advances: Actual one-integer one-continuous-dimensional buffer. This shows changing nondeepest cap credit at fixed parity totals and fixed deepest status. The example has one positive deepest stratum and concerns a buffered objective.

proof:
The canonical hull has real length roof $V_z=\min(1+(1-a)z,\,1+(b-1)z)$ on $[-1,1]$, as follows by linear interpolation between successive sampled intervals and concavity since $a+b<2$. Its centered sections give the stated mass and variance by integrating $x^2$ on an interval of length $v$, which contributes $v^3/12$. The proper closed subsets are the singletons and the two consecutive pairs. The singleton masses are strictly below $M/2=17/16$ except for the stated right endpoint, while each pair uses both parities and misses positive mass. Both roof slopes increase by $t$ under the motion, so it is exactly $V_z(t)=V_z+tz$ with the stated constant masses.

Write $Y=(0,0)$ and $\lambda=L(Y)$. It is an ambient interior point, so concavity supplies an affine supporting majorant $\lambda+c z+q x$. Its nonnegativity at both left endpoints implies $c\le\lambda-a|q|/2$. Its original mixed mean is $\lambda+(b-a)c/M$. Thus
$$
1\le\lambda+\frac{b-a}{M}c\le\lambda\frac{1+2b}{M},
$$
since $b-a>0$. Equality forces $c=\lambda,q=0$ and zero integrated nonnegative gap from the majorant. Continuity gives equality on the sampled intervals. Concavity and the majorant then give equality on their whole convex hull. The displayed $L_*$ is feasible by direct summation and is the only parameter with $L(Y)=M/(1+2b)$.

For a centered interval of length $v$ the ordinary projective energy equals $v(1-4y^2/v^2)$ on the interval. Indeed for an admissible denominator $1+c(x-y)>0$ the integral of its inverse square equals $v/[(1+c(-v/2-y))(1+c(v/2-y))]$. The quadratic product is maximized at $c=-y/(v^2/4-y^2)$ for interior $y$ and both factors there are positive. The given zero extension is the endpoint limit. In particular the shift at $Y$ for $L_*$, after setting $|u|=1$, is $\delta_*=\varepsilon D$. At every mark and for every admissible $L$ the shift is at most $\varepsilon\sqrt{2\Sigma}$. In fact on a sampled interval the area under a nonnegative concave profile with a maximum $m$ is at least $vm/2$, by the two chords to the endpoints, including the limiting one-chord case. Its integral is at most $M$ and $E\le v$, so $LE/M\le2$. Also $\Sigma\le b^2/12\le289/3072<1/9$. Thus the center shift is less than $\varepsilon/2$ and its own cut is proper.

For either orientation at $Y$ and any shift $0\le\delta<1/2$, the own cap length is $1/2+\delta$. The endpoint thresholds range over pairs with mean $-\delta$, because the base coefficient is arbitrary. The clipping identity in the proof of c680a307d3f26cec applies to intervals of lengths $a\le b$ with that mean and gives endpoint infimum $\min\{a,\max(0,(a+b)/2+2\delta)\}=a$. In particular it is attained by a finite tilt filling the smaller interval and missing the larger one. Pure-base caps at $Y$ retain at least $1+a$. The center depth is therefore exactly $1/2+a+\delta$ for every admissible profile. For $L_*$ the particular pair $\pm x-2z\ge-\delta_*$ has these endpoint statuses because $a/2\le1/16$ and $b/2\le17/32$, and its own section is a single point, of zero-dimensional area one, with unit continuous normal.

For another middle mark $y$ under $L_*$, orient the continuous normal toward the nearer endpoint and choose a finite tilt that fills the left interval and misses the right. The resulting mass is at most $a+1/2-|y|+\delta_*\sqrt{1-4y^2}$, strictly less than the center value for $y\ne0$. Indeed the own threshold in the oriented coordinates is $|y|-\delta_*\sqrt{1-4y^2}$, at least $-\delta_*>-1/2$ and at most $1/2$. On either extreme base a finite outward tilt isolates the own fiber. With the nearer continuous orientation the left value is at most $a/2$ because $L_*$ vanishes there. The right value is at most $b/2+\varepsilon\sqrt{2b\Sigma/(1+2b)}\le17/32+\varepsilon/3$. Both are strictly below $1/2+a\ge9/16$. This proves the global maximum and its unique mark. For every other admissible $L$ the lower bound for $L(Y)$ is strict, so the exact center-depth formula gives a strictly larger maximum.

Along the path differentiate $D^2=(a^3+1+b^3)/(12M(1+2b))$, using $a'=-1,b'=1,M'=0$. This gives the displayed logarithmic derivative. Since $b\ge1$, $\Sigma<1/9$ gives $D^2<1/27<1/25$. With $b^2<2$ and $a^3+1+b^3\ge2$, the logarithmic derivative is less than $3/2$, so $D'<3/10$. The two derivatives of the optimized values follow directly. The unchanged cap equations in the same normal scaling capture odd mass exactly $a$, which decreases at rate one although the total odd mass is fixed. The status assertions follow from the unique deepest mark and the profile.
statement:
Let $n=d=1$, $1/16\le a\le1/8$ and $b=9/8-a$. Let $C(a,b)$ be the canonical hull of centered intervals of lengths $a,1,b$ at the integer bases $-1,0,1$. Write $\mu$ for the original mixed length, $M=17/8$, and $\Sigma=(a^3+1+b^3)/(12M)$ for the original volume-weighted within-fiber variance. For $0<\varepsilon\le10^{-4}$, let $L$ range over continuous nonnegative concave parameters on $C(a,b)$ with $\int L\,d\mu=M$. Use the ordinary interval projective energy $E_z(y)$, with value zero at the own endpoints, and the arithmetic buffer
$$
\varepsilon\sqrt{\Sigma}\,|u|\sqrt{L(z,y)E_z(y)/M}
$$
subtracted from the through-mark threshold for a cap with continuous coefficient $u$. Pure-base containing caps are unchanged. Equivalently, a unit continuous normal gives the displayed physical shift without the factor $|u|$. The unique parameter minimizing the maximum raw buffered depth is $L_*(z,y)=M(1+z)/(1+2b)$. Its unique deepest mark is $(0,0)$ and its exact maximum is $Q_\varepsilon=1/2+a+\varepsilon D$, where $D=\sqrt{\Sigma/(1+2b)}$ and $\beta_\varepsilon=Q_\varepsilon/M$.

On the actual path $(a_t,b_t)=(a-t,b+t)$ while $a_t$ stays in range, the sampled even and odd masses stay $1,9/8$, respectively, and the real length roof changes by $tz$. At the current parameters
$$
\frac{D'}D=\frac12\left[\frac{3(b^2-a^2)}{a^3+1+b^3}-\frac{2}{1+2b}\right],\qquad
Q_\varepsilon'<-1+\frac{3\varepsilon}{10}<0,\qquad
\beta_\varepsilon'=Q_\varepsilon'/M.
$$
The caps $\pm x-2z\ge-\varepsilon D$ attain the depth at $(0,0)$ and each has own coarea one in this scaling. Each fully captures the zero-$L$ left fiber and misses the positive-$L$ right fiber, so its odd-parity credit decreases at rate one with the fixed parity mass. The only deepest base is $0$, in the positive-$L$ class. All nonempty proper closed-minor quotas $\sum_{z\in B}V_z<M k(B)/2$ are strict for $a>1/16$, and at $a=1/16$ only the right singleton meets equality. Here $B$ ranges over sampled subsets closed under taking the sampled convex hull, and $k(B)$ counts their occupied base parities.
title: Signed interval-roof descent at fixed total and parity masses
